summary: Hsueh-li Cheng works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Ohio University from circa 1974 to 1976 and at the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo from circa 1976 to 2010.

Hu Shi was a philosopher, sinologist, and historian. He studied at Cornell University and earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor John Dewey, also learning under Kaiten Nukariya. He was president of Peking University in 1946 and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).

Huabei Tan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Tan pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under doctoral supervisor Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

Huai-Chin Nan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and the University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. His career included teaching at the ROC Military Academy, National Chengchi University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Chinese Culture University.

Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, later serving as assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (circa 2007–2013).

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University, the University of Tokyo, and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Hubert Decleer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Alliance Française, SIT Graduate Institute, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

Hubert Durt was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He served as professor and editor-in-chief at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, director of the Hōbōgirin Institute, and held professorships at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and IIBS.

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wendy Doniger, and in 1998 held a post as Associate Professor in Comparative Studies at Ohio State University.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Keble College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1930–1950) and was later an Honorary Fellow at the British Academy (1952) and Keble College (1981).

Hugh Gray was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he served as a lecturer at SOAS University of London and the University of London from circa 1964 to 1982.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Stanford University. He was a longtime professor at Stony Brook University from 1974, executive director of the IAPL, and held visiting chairs and appointments at the University of Vienna, AFA Vienna, Stanford, Klagenfurt, and Turin.

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études and trained under several traditional teachers. He held a Newton International Fellowship at the University of Cambridge before becoming a permanent member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.

Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada around 1956 and held a post at Sophia University from circa 1935 to 1940.
Huidi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor at the National Taiwan University of Arts, executive director at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and president of Dharma Drum Buddhist College (circa 2007–2014).
Huishan Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Lin completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Guowei Liu, and also studied under teachers Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar. Zhuang earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard University. He taught at Harvard before joining the University of Chicago in 1994, with appointments also at NYU, Oxford, and the Smart Museum of Art.
